goal.sentence: Write a program that asks your name and greets you.

steps.instruction: Make a new file named hello.py.
steps.why: Python programs live in files whose names end in .py.
hints: Files live in the Explorer, on the left of VS Code.
Point at the folder's name and click the New File icon.
Click New File, type hello.py, then press Enter.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: that file is hello.txt. Python files end in .py: rename it hello.py.
Not yet: that file is helo.py. Check the spelling: rename it hello.py.

steps.instruction: On line 1, type print("Hello, world!") and save.
steps.why: print shows text in the terminal when the program runs.
hints: print( ) shows whatever you put inside its brackets.
Words go inside quotes, and the quotes go inside the brackets.
Type print("Hello, world!") on line 1, then save with Ctrl+S.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: Python reads capitals exactly. Write print with a small p.
Not yet: print needs brackets around the words: print("Hello, world!")

steps.instruction: On line 2, type name = "Asha" and save.
steps.why: A variable keeps a value, so later lines can use it.
hints: A variable is a name that holds a value.
The variable goes left of =, its value goes right, in quotes.
Type name = "Asha" on line 2. Your own name works too.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: you wrote Name. Capitals matter: write name, all small letters.
Not yet: you wrote nmae. Check the spelling: write name.

steps.instruction: On line 3, print a greeting using name, then save.
steps.why: An f before the quotes tells Python to fill in {name}.
hints: print can show a variable, not only fixed words.
Put f before the quotes and name in curly brackets: {name}.
Type print(f"Nice to meet you, {name}!") on line 3.

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: put f before the quotes, so Python fills in {name}.
Not yet: inside the curly brackets, write name with a small n.

steps.instruction: Make line 2 ask for the name with input, then save.
steps.why: input waits for someone to type, so everyone gets their own greeting.

args.text:
print("Hello, world!")
name = input("What is your name? ")
print(f"Nice to meet you, {name}!")

hints: input( ) asks a question and waits for the answer.
Replace "Asha" with input( ), and put the question in quotes.
Make line 2 read name = input("What is your name? ")

mistakes.not_yet: Not yet: input needs brackets to run: input("What is your name? ")

steps.instruction: Run hello.py, then type your name in the terminal.
steps.why: Running it is how you see your program work.
hints: Save the file first, then run it.
Click the Run button at the top right of the editor.
Or type python hello.py in the terminal and press Enter.
